title: Choosing the sub-jobs yourself
idea: MEET: given a fresh task, pick a sensible set of named sub-jobs. No code.

exercises.prompt: NEW TASK: 'Run a short quiz: ask three questions, count the right answers, then show the score.' A good first sub-job is...
exercises.explanation: Reading in order, asking the questions comes first. You pick the sub-jobs by following the task's order.

exercises.prompt: Order the three sub-jobs of that quiz task.
exercises.explanation: Ask, then count, then show. The sub-jobs run in the order the task describes.

exercises.prompt: NEW TASK: 'Print a star border, print a title, print the same star border again.' Which sub-job REPEATS?
exercises.explanation: The border job appears at the top and bottom - it repeats. That's the job worth naming once.

exercises.prompt: For the border task, which named sub-jobs make sense? (Pick all.)
exercises.explanation: The border and the title are the real jobs. The other two have nothing to do with the task.

exercises.prompt: NEW TASK: 'For each player, greet them and show their score.' What's the repeated set of jobs?
options: greet + show score, once per player
exercises.explanation: For every player you greet and show a score - a repeated pair of jobs. Repetition says 'reuse me'.

exercises.prompt: Match each new task to a sensible sub-job inside it.
exercises.explanation: Given any task, you can now name its sub-jobs. That's the planning skill of this whole unit.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: the quiz sub-job 'count the right answers' uses which tool?
exercises.explanation: 'Count the right answers' tallies the ones that pass the test - a count with a condition.

exercises.prompt: There can be more than one reasonable way to split a task into sub-jobs.
exercises.explanation: True. Different sensible splits can all work, as long as each sub-job is clear and the parts cover the task.

options: Each sub-job is clear, and together they do the whole task
It has exactly one job always
exercises.explanation: A good split covers the whole task with clear, named jobs - none missing, none vague.

exercises.prompt: You can now take a fresh task and...
options: name a sensible set of sub-jobs, in order, spotting any repeats
exercises.explanation: That's the goal of this MEET unit: read a task and decompose it into named sub-jobs - ready to code next.
